attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his signed newsletter post, written in his voice. He is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: Keeps all four stated effects and the 'in turn' chain. It correctly leaves out the motive framing from the surrounding sentence. The claim states the mechanism outright, with no hedge.

contract.note: Zitron names no metric. Reading 'more reasons to interact' as added opportunities to interact, not a measured rise in engagement, is the ordinary reading of how he describes the mechanism. It is not stretched either way. A test of net engagement would turn this into a claim he did not make.

evidence.note: Meta's own product announcement, dated 2023-12-06, so before the post. It describes asking the assistant questions, generating and sharing images, and a 'reimagine' feature that lets a friend remix a generated image in group chat. That matches the support condition. It is a company disclosure, but the contract asks for product documentation.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's plain reading, the claim is that the assistant opened new ways to create content and for other users to respond to it. Meta's December 2023 documentation shows exactly that: Q&A, image creation and sharing, and friends remixing images in group chat, all before the May 2024 post. The packet has no counterevidence. The claim is not scored for any net increase in engagement, since Zitron did not claim one.
